text: {"headline":"The 99215 share is far above expectation in every complexity band, including patients with no or one chronic condition, but documentation is too thin to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 share appears even among 0–1 condition patients, at roughly nine and five times the all-provider rate. Sampled low-complexity 99215 claims such as C0047252 (Z09 only), C0048364 (J06.9) and C0047606 (R21) carry diagnoses that would not usually support high-complexity visits, so the billing pattern is consistent with upcoding and not simply a sicker panel. The records review cuts the other way but carries little weight: the few documented 99215 claims (e.g., C0047267, C0047450) all supported the billed level. Documentation covers only about 2% of claims, and the two below-billed findings were 99214s (C0047208, C0048357) documented at low MDM. The handful of moderate-plus data-reviewed notes without a lab or test line is weak evidence of possible note inflation, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet, then check whether those notes show genuine high-complexity MDM or time, or templated content."}
